title: Use cookbook_lookup
text:
Tool: cookbook_lookup
Display alias: cookbook.lookup
Purpose: Search structured electronics cookbook cards for topology candidates, design equations, tool-aware recipes, validation criteria, failure modes, and capability gaps.
When to use: Use before choosing a circuit topology, when translating requirements into a design procedure, when deciding what analysis/instruments are required, when debugging why a design failed, or when checking whether the app has the necessary tools. Do not use cookbook knowledge as proof that a particular circuit works; proof must come from app tools, solver data, or instrument data.
Result: Returns matching card IDs, titles, tokens, provenance/source path, priority, and recipe summary text.

title: Use cookbook_coverage
text:
Tool: cookbook_coverage
Display alias: cookbook.coverage
Purpose: Report cookbook coverage against the file-backed taxonomy derived from the comprehensive electronics cookbook goal.
When to use: Use when planning cookbook development, checking whether a domain already has recipe coverage, selecting the next cookbook expansion area, or reporting capability progress. Coverage is a map, not proof of engineering completeness inside a category.
Result: Returns required category count, covered category count, missing categories, coverage ratio, and cookbook entry IDs per category.

title: Use cookbook_validate
text:
Tool: cookbook_validate
Display alias: cookbook.validate
Purpose: Validate cookbook entries for structured-field completeness, taxonomy alignment, duplicate IDs, malformed raw entries, and retrieval-quality warnings.
When to use: Use after adding or editing cookbook cards, before claiming cookbook data is clean, or when debugging cookbook retrieval/coverage anomalies. Passing validation does not prove the electronics knowledge is complete or experimentally verified; it proves the card structure is usable by the agent.
Result: Returns status, cookbook entry count, error count, warning count, and arrays of validation findings.

title: Use cookbook_acceptance_goals
text:
Tool: cookbook_acceptance_goals
Display alias: cookbook.acceptance_goals
Purpose: List representative agent acceptance goals, including required cookbook retrieval, tool evidence, expected capability gaps, and pass criteria.
When to use: Use when selecting an acceptance/regression goal, checking how to validate agent behavior across engineering domains, or filtering the goal suite by domain or exact goal id.
Result: Returns required acceptance domains and matching structured goal objects from COOKBOOK_ACCEPTANCE_GOALS.json.

title: Use cookbook_acceptance_summary
text:
Tool: cookbook_acceptance_summary
Display alias: cookbook.acceptance_summary
Purpose: Summarize generated acceptance run reports, including status, final determination, report paths, evidence counts, required evidence counts, and readiness flags.
When to use: Use before rerunning acceptance goals, when checking progress across domains, when deciding which reports need more retrieved cards/tool evidence/criteria results, or when auditing whether claims have durable artifacts.
Result: Reads sim/xyce/runs/generated/acceptance/**/acceptance_report.json and returns compact run summaries with evidenceReadiness scores, optionally filtered by domain or exact goal id.

title: Use cookbook_acceptance_start
text:
Tool: cookbook_acceptance_start
Display alias: cookbook.acceptance_start
Purpose: Create a durable acceptance-run report scaffold for a representative goal id, including checklist sections for cookbook retrieval, tool evidence, pass criteria, expected capability gaps, and evidence notes.
When to use: Use before executing a representative acceptance goal so the run has a structured evidence container. The scaffold is not proof of success; it is the place to record tool-derived evidence and capability gaps.
Result: Writes acceptance_report.json and acceptance_report.md under the generated acceptance run directory and returns their paths.

title: Use cookbook_acceptance_record
text:
Tool: cookbook_acceptance_record
Display alias: cookbook.acceptance_record
Purpose: Append structured evidence to an acceptance report created by cookbook_acceptance_start.
When to use: Use during representative acceptance goals after retrieving cookbook cards, running app tools, generating artifacts, checking criteria, or discovering a capability gap. Record what the tool actually produced instead of relying on chat transcript memory.
Result: Updates acceptance_report.json and appends a human-readable evidence line to acceptance_report.md. Evidence types include retrieved_card, tool_call, artifact, capability_gap, criterion, and note.

title: Use capability_gap_record
text:
Tool: capability_gap_record
Display alias: capability_gap.record
Purpose: Append a reusable missing-capability record to the project gap registry.
When to use: Use when a cookbook step, acceptance goal, solver claim, plot, model, instrument workflow, or UI operation cannot be completed with current app tools. Record the reusable capability needed to close the gap instead of fabricating evidence or burying the gap in chat.
Result: Appends a JSONL record to projects/current/.djehuti/CAPABILITY_GAPS.jsonl and returns the registry path plus generated gap id.

title: Use circuit_run_erc
text:
Tool: circuit_run_erc
Display alias: circuit.run_erc
Purpose: Run Electrical Rule Check on the current schematic model.
When to use: Use before solver-backed analysis, when the user asks whether the circuit is electrically sane, or when debugging missing ground, floating pins, duplicate reference designators, source shorts, unsupported primitives, or missing probes.
Result: Returns JSON with status, error count, warning count, and report path. The markdown report is written to the generated run folder.

title: Use simulation_export_artifacts
text:
Tool: simulation_export_artifacts
Display alias: simulation.export_artifacts
Purpose: Export the current circuit JSON, generated Xyce netlist, lab instrument JSON, and assistant tool manifest.
When to use: Use when preparing solver runs, debugging generated files, handing circuit state to another process, or making the model visible outside the UI.
Result: Returns JSON with paths to circuit.json, generated.cir, lab_instruments.json, and assistant_tools.json.

title: Use filter_design_high_pass
text:
Tool: filter_design_high_pass
Display alias: filter.design_high_pass
Purpose: Design and draw a matched second-order RLC high-pass filter, run the built-in AC sweep, and export response graph/data artifacts.
When to use: Use when the user asks for a matched RLC high-pass filter with cutoff and impedance requirements, especially the 10 Hz / 8 Ohm acceptance-style task. Still run or inspect ERC evidence before making solver-backed claims when the schematic has been modified manually.
Result: Updates the schematic model and returns paths for generated analysis artifacts, including response data and graph outputs from the tool.

title: Use circuit_inspect
text:
Tool: circuit_inspect
Display alias: circuit.inspect
Purpose: Read the current authoritative circuit model as JSON without modifying it.
When to use: Use before explaining a schematic, proposing edits, choosing test equipment, or deciding which analysis to run.
Result: Returns the current circuit JSON. The circuit model is authoritative; the screen drawing is an editable view over that model.

title: Use schematic_place_symbol
text:
Tool: schematic_place_symbol
Display alias: schematic.place_symbol
Purpose: Place a schematic symbol or instrument node at a grid coordinate.
When to use: Use when the user asks the assistant to create or modify a diagram. Instrument nodes such as oscilloscope_2ch and digital_multimeter should be placed this way, then wired like normal components.
Layout rule: create readable schematics with signal flow left-to-right. Put sources on the left, processing parts in the middle, loads/outputs on the right, grounds below the parts they reference, and instruments to the far right. Keep symbols at least 144 px apart horizontally or 96 px apart vertically. Never reuse the same x/y coordinate for multiple parts. Unsupported symbols are rejected; do not pretend a resistor is a transistor.
Result: Returns the placed reference designator, symbol id, and snapped coordinates.

title: Use schematic_connect
text:
Tool: schematic_connect
Display alias: schematic.connect
Purpose: Connect two schematic pins or junctions by label.
When to use: Use after placing components or instruments when the user asks for a diagram or circuit topology. Labels look like R1.1, R1.2, V2.+, V2.-, GND3.0, SCOPE4.CH1, SCOPE4.REF, DMM5.HI, or N1 (junction).
Result: Returns whether the wire was created, the resolved node labels, and total wire count.

title: Use instrument_open_panel
text:
Tool: instrument_open_panel
Display alias: instrument.open_panel
Purpose: Open the floating instrument panel for an existing wired schematic instrument node.
When to use: Use only when the user explicitly asks to open or show a scope, DMM, or other instrument panel. Do not use during normal AI circuit creation; place and wire instrument nodes on the schematic instead. In this system users open panels by double-clicking instrument nodes.
Result: Returns the opened instrument reference designator, symbol id, and connected pin count.

Tool: schematic_auto_layout
Display alias: schematic.auto_layout
Purpose: Automatically arrange the current schematic into a readable left-to-right diagram using standard spacing conventions.
When to use: Use after placing or wiring components, when the user asks for auto layout, when components overlap, or before presenting a generated circuit. The first implementation lays out the current diagram by component role; future versions will support selection scope and block-specific styles.
Result: Updates component coordinates and returns component count and layout style.
title: Use schematic_auto_layout

text:
Tool: schematic_auto_layout_selection
Display alias: schematic.auto_layout_selection
Purpose: Automatically arrange only the currently selected schematic components.
When to use: Use after box-selecting or shift-selecting a pile of parts that should be cleaned up without disturbing the rest of the diagram. If nothing is selected, use schematic_auto_layout for the full diagram or select components first.
Result: Updates selected component coordinates and returns component count and layout style.
title: Use schematic_auto_layout_selection
Use agent_write_markdown
text:
Tool: agent_write_markdown
Display alias: agent.write_markdown
Purpose: Write a markdown report into the agent workspace and render it in the BYOK Agent window with KaTeX equation support.
When to use: Use for equation-rich derivations, design notes, validation reports, acceptance notes, or user-readable explanations that should be rendered instead of left as raw chat text.
Equation syntax: use $...$ for inline math and $$ on separate lines before and after display equations. Use KaTeX equations for filters, transfer functions, impedance, gain, cutoff frequency, component sizing, and other math-heavy design reasoning.
Result: Writes markdown and rendered HTML files and updates the BYOK Agent conversation.

title: Use research_web_search
text:
Tool: research_web_search
Display alias: research.web_search
Purpose: Search the web for current external references, standards, datasheets, source links, or facts not available in the local cookbook/app state.
When to use: Use sparingly when external source attribution or current information matters. Prefer circuit_inspect, cookbook_lookup, and local tool outputs for current circuit facts. Treat search snippets as leads; do not overclaim without checking source quality.
Result: Returns compact title/snippet/url entries.

title: Use schematic_group_create
text:
Tool: schematic_group_create
Display alias: schematic.group_create
Purpose: Draw a named group box around existing components.
When to use: Use when the user asks to group, box, frame, or label a section of the schematic (for example the output stage or bias network). Pass a name and the member reference designators. Group boxes only label a region; wiring and the circuit do not change. The name appears in the box's top-left corner.
Result: Returns the new group with its id (G1, G2...), name, category, notes, and members.

title: Use schematic_group_update
text:
Tool: schematic_group_update
Display alias: schematic.group_update
Purpose: Rename a group box or change its members, category, or notes.
When to use: Use when the user asks to rename a group or add/remove components from it. Identify the group by id or name; omitted fields stay unchanged.
Result: Returns the updated group.

title: Use schematic_group_delete
text:
Tool: schematic_group_delete
Display alias: schematic.group_delete
Purpose: Remove a group box without touching its components.
When to use: Use when the user asks to ungroup or remove a group box. Components and wiring stay exactly as they are.
Result: Returns the removed group.

title: Use schematic_group_list
text:
Tool: schematic_group_list
Display alias: schematic.group_list
Purpose: List the group boxes on the schematic.
When to use: Use before updating or deleting a group when you need its id, or when the user asks what groups exist.
Result: Returns every group with id, name, category, notes, and member reference designators.

title: Use schematic_subdiagram_create
text:
Tool: schematic_subdiagram_create
Display alias: schematic.subdiagram_create
Purpose: Fold components into a sub-diagram block.
When to use: Use when the user wants part of a complex schematic shown as a block (for example 'make the output stage a sub-diagram'). Pass a name plus member reference designators, or an existing group. Signal nets crossing the boundary become block pins named IN, OUT, IN2... (or the net label name); ground and named supplies stay global. Inside, each pin is a port bubble with the pin name, and the inner sheet is auto-laid out. Blocks can be nested by folding parts on a block's own sheet.
Result: Returns the block refdes (A1...), name, pins with sides, and members.

title: Use schematic_subdiagram_expand
text:
Tool: schematic_subdiagram_expand
Display alias: schematic.subdiagram_expand
Purpose: Unfold a sub-diagram block back onto its parent sheet.
When to use: Use when the user wants a block's parts shown inline again. The parts return centred on the block position inside a group box with the block's name.
Result: Returns the expanded block, the sheet, and the new group id.

title: Use schematic_subdiagram_open
text:
Tool: schematic_subdiagram_open
Display alias: schematic.subdiagram_open
Purpose: Change which sheet is viewed and edited.
When to use: Use to work inside a block (target = block refdes or name), to go up a level ('up'), or back to the top ('main'). Placement, wiring, auto layout, and group tools then act on that sheet.
Result: Returns the sheet being viewed and the path from the main sheet.

title: Use schematic_subdiagram_rename
text:
Tool: schematic_subdiagram_rename
Display alias: schematic.subdiagram_rename
Purpose: Rename a sub-diagram block.
When to use: Use when the user asks to rename a block.
Result: Returns the updated block.

title: Use schematic_subdiagram_rename_port
text:
Tool: schematic_subdiagram_rename_port
Display alias: schematic.subdiagram_rename_port
Purpose: Rename a block pin and its port bubble together.
When to use: Use when generic pin names like IN or OUT2 should become meaningful (for example DRIVE or SPEAKER).
Result: Returns the updated block with its pins.

title: Use schematic_subdiagram_expose_parameter
text:
Tool: schematic_subdiagram_expose_parameter
Display alias: schematic.subdiagram_expose_parameter
Purpose: Explicitly expose an internal component parameter on a sub-diagram block so it appears in the block Properties panel and can be set from outside.
When to use: Use after making a reusable sub-diagram when the user chooses which internal values should be configurable. Pass the block, outside parameterName, internal targetRefdes, and targetParameter key. Do not infer or expose parameters automatically without user intent.
Result: Returns the updated block and exposed parameter name.

title: Use schematic_subdiagram_list
text:
Tool: schematic_subdiagram_list
Display alias: schematic.subdiagram_list
Purpose: List sub-diagram blocks.
When to use: Use to find block refdes, pins, members, or which sheet is being viewed before opening, renaming, or expanding.
Result: Returns every block with name, parent sheet, pins, and members, plus the viewed sheet.

title: Use library_save_block
text:
Tool: library_save_block
Display alias: library.save_block
Purpose: Save a finished sub-diagram block into the user's reusable circuit-block library.
When to use: Use after creating a useful circuit module as a sub-diagram and the user wants to reuse it later. Saved blocks are copy templates, not linked definitions: placing one creates a new editable sub-diagram copy with its own internal sheet(s).
Result: Returns the saved library block name, file path, and source block summary.

title: Use library_list_blocks
text:
Tool: library_list_blocks
Display alias: library.list_blocks
Purpose: List reusable circuit blocks saved in the user's library.
When to use: Use before placing a library module, or when the user asks what reusable circuits are available. The optional query filters by name, category, description, or source metadata.
Result: Returns saved block names, categories, descriptions, and file paths.

title: Use library_place_block
text:
Tool: library_place_block
Display alias: library.place_block
Purpose: Place a reusable library block onto the current sheet as a fresh editable copy.
When to use: Use when the user wants to drop a saved circuit module as a node/block. The placed block is independent: double-click/open it to edit its copied internal diagram without changing the saved library template or other placed copies.
Result: Returns the new sub-diagram block refdes, name, pins, child sheet, and copied members.

title: Use schematic_export_image
text:
Tool: schematic_export_image
Display alias: schematic.export_image
Purpose: Render a schematic sheet to a PNG exactly as drawn.
When to use: Use to check a drawing's readability after layout changes, or when the user asks for an image of the main sheet or a sub-diagram.
Result: Returns the sheet name and the PNG path.

title: Use project_create
text:
Tool: project_create
Display alias: project.create
Purpose: Create a named project.
When to use: Use when the user wants a new project. A project is a named folder of named diagrams; it defaults to Documents\Djehuti Electronics Lab\Projects. Follow with diagram_create for its first diagram.
Result: Returns the open project.

title: Use project_open
text:
Tool: project_open
Display alias: project.open
Purpose: Open a project.
When to use: Use when the user names a project to work on, by name or folder path. The current diagram is saved first and the project's last diagram opens.
Result: Returns the open project.

title: Use project_list
text:
Tool: project_list
Display alias: project.list
Purpose: List projects.
When to use: Use to find a project by name or see what exists.
Result: Returns known projects and the open project.

title: Use project_info
text:
Tool: project_info
Display alias: project.info
Purpose: Show the open project.
When to use: Use to check the project name, folder, diagrams, the open diagram, or unsaved changes.
Result: Returns project details.

title: Use project_rename
text:
Tool: project_rename
Display alias: project.rename
Purpose: Rename the open project.
When to use: Use when the user renames the project; the folder is renamed too.
Result: Returns the renamed project.

title: Use diagram_create
text:
Tool: diagram_create
Display alias: diagram.create
Purpose: Create a named blank diagram.
When to use: Use when the user wants a new diagram in the open project. It is saved blank immediately and opened.
Result: Returns the project with its diagrams.

title: Use diagram_open
text:
Tool: diagram_open
Display alias: diagram.open
Purpose: Open a diagram.
When to use: Use to switch to another diagram of the open project. The current one is saved first.
Result: Returns the project with the open diagram.

title: Use diagram_list
text:
Tool: diagram_list
Display alias: diagram.list
Purpose: List the project's diagrams.
When to use: Use to see which diagrams exist and which is open.
Result: Returns the project's diagrams.

title: Use diagram_save
text:
Tool: diagram_save
Display alias: diagram.save
Purpose: Save the open diagram.
When to use: Use when the user asks to save. Saves every sheet, sub-diagram, group and wire of the open diagram.
Result: Returns the project.

title: Use diagram_save_as
text:
Tool: diagram_save_as
Display alias: diagram.save_as
Purpose: Save the diagram under a new name.
When to use: Use when the user wants a copy to keep working on under another name; the copy becomes the open diagram.
Result: Returns the project.

title: Use diagram_rename
text:
Tool: diagram_rename
Display alias: diagram.rename
Purpose: Rename a diagram.
When to use: Use when the user renames a diagram (the open one by default).
Result: Returns the project.

title: Use diagram_duplicate
text:
Tool: diagram_duplicate
Display alias: diagram.duplicate
Purpose: Duplicate a diagram.
When to use: Use to copy a saved diagram to a new name without opening the copy.
Result: Returns the project.

title: Use diagram_delete
text:
Tool: diagram_delete
Display alias: diagram.delete
Purpose: Remove a diagram from the project.
When to use: Use when the user asks to delete a diagram; its file moves to the project's deleted folder, nothing is erased.
Result: Returns the project.

title: Use instrument_read
text:
Tool: instrument_read
Display alias: instrument.read
Purpose: Read an instrument node the way its window shows it.
When to use: After placing and wiring a scope, multimeter, or frequency analyzer, to get its measurements: scope Vpp/Vrms/mean/frequency per channel, meter reading in its function, analyzer peak gain and -3 dB points. Change its settings (time_per_div, ch1_volts_per_div, trigger_level, meter function in value, start_frequency/stop_frequency) with schematic_set_parameters.
Result: Returns the measurements as JSON.

title: Use schematic_get_parameters
text:
Tool: schematic_get_parameters
Display alias: schematic.get_parameters
Purpose: List a part's editable properties.
When to use: Use before changing a part to learn its property keys, current values, units and choices (the Properties pane's fields).
Result: Returns the part type, rotation, sheet, and each property's key/label/value/unit/options.

title: Use schematic_set_parameters
text:
Tool: schematic_set_parameters
Display alias: schematic.set_parameters
Purpose: Change a part's properties.
When to use: Use to set component values (resistance, capacitance), source waveform/amplitude/frequency/offset, transistor or diode models, switch states, supply and label names, and instrument settings (scope time_per_div, ch1_volts_per_div, trigger_level; meter function in value; analyzer start_frequency/stop_frequency). Values accept 4.7k, 10u, 1meg.
Result: Returns the part's updated properties, or why a value was rejected.

title: Use schematic_rename_component
text:
Tool: schematic_rename_component
Display alias: schematic.rename_component
Purpose: Rename a part's reference designator.
When to use: Use when the user wants a different refdes (for example RL1 to RLOAD).
Result: Returns the new refdes.

title: Use schematic_rotate_component
text:
Tool: schematic_rotate_component
Display alias: schematic.rotate_component
Purpose: Rotate a part.
When to use: Use to set a part's rotation to 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees.
Result: Returns the new rotation.

title: Use schematic_convert_supply
text:
Tool: schematic_convert_supply
Display alias: schematic.convert_supply
Purpose: Switch a supply or ground between a rail and per-pin symbols.
When to use: When the user wants a power or ground bus drawn as a rail, or as individual supply ports / ground symbols at each pin. Pass a rail refdes with to=symbols, or any port/ground symbol with to=rail. The circuit does not change.
Result: Returns what was converted.

title: Use preferences_list
text:
Tool: preferences_list
Display alias: preferences.list
Purpose: List the user's preferences.
When to use: Use to find a preference key or check its value, optionally with a search word (rail, spacing, grid, label, units, projects).
Result: Returns matching preferences with key, category, label, value, choices and description.

title: Use preferences_set
text:
Tool: preferences_set
Display alias: preferences.set
Purpose: Change a user preference.
When to use: Use only when the user asks to change how the app behaves or looks, for example 'keep my rails when laying out' (layout.supply_symbols=false), 'roomier layout' (layout.spacing=Roomy), 'dot grid' (display.grid=Dots), 'M means milli' (units.capital_m=Milli (SPICE)).
Result: Returns the key and its new value.

title: Use schematic_delete_components
text:
Tool: schematic_delete_components
Display alias: schematic.delete_components
Purpose: Delete components and the wires attached to them.
When to use: The user asks to remove parts, or a part was placed by mistake. Blocks must be expanded first.
Result: Returns the reference designators deleted.

title: Use analytics_list
text:
Tool: analytics_list
Display alias: analytics.list
Purpose: List what can be analysed on the open diagram.
When to use: Use first when you need net names, input sources or sweepable parameters (R1.value, V1.dc, Q1.beta, TEMP) for an analytics tool.
Result: Every analysis with its settings, the nets with their pins, the sources and the sweep targets.
Note: analytics tools never change the diagram; they simulate it as it is.

title: Use analytics_operating_point
text:
Tool: analytics_operating_point
Display alias: analytics.operating_point
Purpose: DC operating point (.OP).
When to use: Use for bias questions: node voltages, currents, power, transistor region, gm, r_pi, r_o.
Result: Tables of node voltages, sources, element currents and power, and one table per device.
Note: analytics tools never change the diagram; they simulate it as it is.

title: Use analytics_dc_sweep
text:
Tool: analytics_dc_sweep
Display alias: analytics.dc_sweep
Purpose: DC sweep (.DC).
When to use: Use to plot node voltages or currents while a source, a part value or temperature is swept; nested with step_target.
Result: Curves per output, end points; CSV files.
Note: analytics tools never change the diagram; they simulate it as it is.

title: Use analytics_ac
text:
Tool: analytics_ac
Display alias: analytics.ac
Purpose: AC small-signal sweep (.AC).
When to use: Use for frequency response, Bode plots, bandwidth, -3 dB corners, unity gain, phase margin; step_target overlays part values.
Result: Magnitude, phase and group delay curves plus an AC summary table.
Note: analytics tools never change the diagram; they simulate it as it is.

title: Use analytics_transient
text:
Tool: analytics_transient
Display alias: analytics.transient
Purpose: Transient (.TRAN).
When to use: Use for time-domain waveforms; stop/step auto by default; outputs may include I(part).
Result: Waveforms per output and min/max/pp/avg/rms/frequency statistics.
Note: analytics tools never change the diagram; they simulate it as it is.

title: Use analytics_fourier
text:
Tool: analytics_fourier
Display alias: analytics.fourier
Purpose: Fourier / THD (.FOUR).
When to use: Use for harmonic distortion of a node's steady-state waveform.
Result: Harmonic table (magnitude, normalized, phase), THD and a harmonics bar chart.
Note: analytics tools never change the diagram; they simulate it as it is.

title: Use analytics_noise
text:
Tool: analytics_noise
Display alias: analytics.noise
Purpose: Noise (.NOISE).
When to use: Use for output and input-referred noise density, integrated noise and which parts contribute it.
Result: Noise density curves, integrated rms totals, per-element contributions.
Note: analytics tools never change the diagram; they simulate it as it is.

title: Use analytics_transfer_function
text:
Tool: analytics_transfer_function
Display alias: analytics.transfer_function
Purpose: Transfer function (.TF).
When to use: Use for small-signal DC gain from a source to an output with input and output resistance.
Result: Gain, Rin, Rout.
Note: analytics tools never change the diagram; they simulate it as it is.

title: Use analytics_sensitivity
text:
Tool: analytics_sensitivity
Display alias: analytics.sensitivity
Purpose: Sensitivity (.SENS).
When to use: Use to find which parts matter most for a DC output (mode DC) or an AC gain at a frequency (mode AC).
Result: Per-parameter derivative and change per +1 %, ranked.
Note: analytics tools never change the diagram; they simulate it as it is.

title: Use analytics_pole_zero
text:
Tool: analytics_pole_zero
Display alias: analytics.pole_zero
Purpose: Pole-zero (.PZ).
When to use: Use for poles, zeros, damping, Q and stability of a transfer function.
Result: Pole and zero tables (rad/s, Hz, zeta, Q) and an s-plane plot.
Note: analytics tools never change the diagram; they simulate it as it is.

title: Use analytics_temperature
text:
Tool: analytics_temperature
Display alias: analytics.temperature
Purpose: Temperature sweep (.TEMP).
When to use: Use for drift of node voltages or currents over a temperature range.
Result: Curves versus temperature and a table; average drift per degree.
Note: analytics tools never change the diagram; they simulate it as it is.

title: Use analytics_monte_carlo
text:
Tool: analytics_monte_carlo
Display alias: analytics.monte_carlo
Purpose: Monte Carlo / tolerance.
When to use: Use for production spread of a DC voltage, TF gain, AC gain or -3 dB corner with part tolerances.
Result: Histogram, mean, standard deviation, min/max, +/-3 sigma, runs.
Note: analytics tools never change the diagram; they simulate it as it is.

title: Use analytics_measure
text:
Tool: analytics_measure
Display alias: analytics.measure
Purpose: Measure a trace of the latest result (.MEAS).
When to use: Use after a run for rise time, overshoot, settling, frequency, RMS, -3 dB, unity gain, phase or gain margin of one trace.
Result: The measured value; also listed in the Analytics window.
Note: analytics tools never change the diagram; they simulate it as it is.

title: Use analytics_result
text:
Tool: analytics_result
Display alias: analytics.result
Purpose: Return a stored Analytics result again.
When to use: Use to re-read the latest (index 0) or an earlier result without re-running.
Result: The result JSON with settings, summary, tables, traces and files.
Note: analytics tools never change the diagram; they simulate it as it is.

title: Use analytics_open
text:
Tool: analytics_open
Display alias: analytics.open
Purpose: Show the Analytics window with an analysis and settings, without running.
When to use: Use when the user wants to set up an analysis to run themselves.
Result: The analysis shown.
Note: analytics tools never change the diagram; they simulate it as it is.

title: Use frust_run
text:
Tool: frust_run
Display alias: frust.run
Purpose: Compile Frust with the embedded compiler and run it in the app.
When to use: Use when the user asks to write or try Frust code, or a calculation is easier as a program. Source defines pub fn run() -> String; print_line(text) adds output lines.
Result: The output, or compile diagnostics with line and column; the code appears in the Frust panel.

title: Use frust_check
text:
Tool: frust_check
Display alias: frust.check
Purpose: Compile Frust without running it.
When to use: Use to check Frust code for errors before running it.
Result: Diagnostics with line and column, or none.
